title.en: I have to, you must, you should
title.de: Pflicht und Rat: have to, must, should
title.sl: Obveznost in nasvet: have to, must, should
title.it: Dovere e consigli: have to, must, should

goal.sl: Poveš, kaj moraš in česa ne smeš (have to, must, mustn't), da nečesa ni treba (don't have to), in daš nasvet (You should take a coat).
goal.de: Du sagst, was du tun musst und was verboten ist (have to, must, mustn't), dass etwas nicht nötig ist (don't have to), und gibst einen Rat (You should take a coat).
goal.it: Dici che cosa devi fare e che cosa non è permesso (have to, must, mustn't), che qualcosa non è necessario (don't have to), e dai un consiglio (You should take a coat).
goal.en: You can say what you have to do and what is not allowed (have to, must, mustn't), that there is no need (don't have to), and give advice (You should take a coat).

say.sl: **have to** + osnovna oblika: kar moraš, pogosto zaradi dela ali pravila: **I have to feed the lambs.** (Moram nahraniti jagnjeta.) **We have to be there at nine.** (Ob devetih moramo biti tam.) Pri he, she, it: **has to**: **Jack has to get up at five.** (Jack mora vstati ob petih.) Nikoli *Jack have to*.
say.de: **have to** + Grundform: was du tun musst, oft wegen der Arbeit oder einer Regel: **I have to feed the lambs.** (Ich muss die Lämmer füttern.) **We have to be there at nine.** (Wir müssen um neun dort sein.) Bei he, she, it: **has to**: **Jack has to get up at five.** (Jack muss um fünf aufstehen.) Nie *Jack have to*.
say.it: **have to** + la forma base: ciò che devi fare, spesso per il lavoro o per una regola: **I have to feed the lambs.** (Devo dare da mangiare agli agnelli.) **We have to be there at nine.** (Dobbiamo essere lì alle nove.) Con he, she, it: **has to**: **Jack has to get up at five.** (Jack deve alzarsi alle cinque.) Mai *Jack have to*.
say.en: **have to** + the base form: what you need to do, often because of a job or a rule: **I have to feed the lambs.** **We have to be there at nine.** With he, she, it: **has to**: **Jack has to get up at five.** (never *Jack have to get up at five.*)

examples.en: I have to feed the lambs.
examples.it: Devo dare da mangiare agli agnelli.

examples.en: We have to be at the mill at nine.
examples.sl: Ob devetih moramo biti v mlinu.
examples.de: Wir müssen um neun in der Mühle sein.
examples.it: Dobbiamo essere al mulino alle nove.

examples.en: Jack has to get up at five.

rows: Jack has to get up at five.

say.sl: Pri vprašanju rabiš **do** ali **does**: **Do you have to work on Saturday?** (Moraš v soboto delati?) **Yes, I do.** (Ja.) **Does she have to go?** (Mora iti?) **No, she doesn't.** (Ne.) Preteklik je **had to**: **Yesterday I had to walk home.** (Včeraj sem moral{m:|f:a} domov peš.) V govoru Britanci rečejo tudi **have got to**: **I've got to go.** (Moram iti.)
say.de: Bei der Frage brauchst du **do** oder **does**: **Do you have to work on Saturday?** (Musst du am Samstag arbeiten?) **Yes, I do.** (Ja.) **Does she have to go?** (Muss sie gehen?) **No, she doesn't.** (Nein.) Die Vergangenheit ist **had to**: **Yesterday I had to walk home.** (Gestern musste ich zu Fuß heim.) Gesprochen sagt man in Großbritannien auch **have got to**: **I've got to go.** (Ich muss los.)
say.it: Per chiedere usi **do** o **does**: **Do you have to work on Saturday?** (Devi lavorare sabato?) **Yes, I do.** (Sì.) **Does she have to go?** (Deve andare?) **No, she doesn't.** (No.) Il passato è **had to**: **Yesterday I had to walk home.** (Ieri sono dovut{m:o|f:a} tornare a casa a piedi.) A voce i britannici dicono anche **have got to**: **I've got to go.** (Devo andare.)
say.en: To ask, use **do** or **does**: **Do you have to work on Saturday?** **Yes, I do.** **Does she have to go?** **No, she doesn't.** The past is **had to**: **Yesterday I had to walk home.** In talk British people also say **have got to**: **I've got to go.**

examples.en: Do you have to work on Saturday? — Yes, I do.
examples.de: Musst du am Samstag arbeiten? — Ja.

examples.en: Yesterday the bus didn't come, so I had to walk home.
examples.sl: Včeraj avtobusa ni bilo, zato sem moral{m:|f:a} domov peš.
examples.de: Gestern ist der Bus nicht gekommen, also musste ich zu Fuß heim.
examples.it: Ieri l'autobus non è arrivato, così sono dovut{m:o|f:a} tornare a casa a piedi.

say.sl: **must** + osnovna oblika, za vse enako, brez to: **You must close the gate.** (Moraš zapreti vrata.) **Walkers must stay on the path.** (Pohodniki morajo ostati na poti.) **I must call my mother.** (Moram poklicati mamo.) Nikoli *must to*. Je za pravilo na napisu ali za to, kar se tebi zdi nujno. Preteklika nima: **had to**.
say.de: **must** + Grundform, für alle gleich, ohne to: **You must close the gate.** (Du musst das Tor schließen.) **Walkers must stay on the path.** (Wanderer müssen auf dem Weg bleiben.) **I must call my mother.** (Ich muss meine Mutter anrufen.) Nie *must to*. Es steht für eine Regel auf einem Schild oder für das, was dir selbst nötig scheint. Eine Vergangenheit hat es nicht: **had to**.
say.it: **must** + la forma base, uguale per tutti, senza to: **You must close the gate.** (Devi chiudere il cancello.) **Walkers must stay on the path.** (Gli escursionisti devono restare sul sentiero.) **I must call my mother.** (Devo chiamare mia madre.) Mai *must to*. È per una regola su un cartello o per ciò che a te sembra necessario. Non ha il passato: **had to**.
say.en: **must** + the base form, the same for everyone, with no to: **You must close the gate.** **Walkers must stay on the path.** **I must call** (never *I must to call*). It is for a rule on a notice, or for what you yourself feel is needed. It has no past: **had to**.

examples.en: Walkers must stay on the path.
examples.de: Wanderer müssen auf dem Weg bleiben.
examples.it: Gli escursionisti devono restare sul sentiero.

examples.en: I must call my mother tonight.
examples.de: Heute Abend muss ich meine Mutter anrufen.

say.sl: **mustn't** (must not) pomeni, da ni dovoljeno, ne smeš: **You mustn't feed the horses.** (Konj ne smeš hraniti.) **You mustn't smoke in the barn.** (V skednju ne smeš kaditi.) **We mustn't be late.** (Ne smemo zamuditi.) **can't** pogosto pove isto: **You can't park here.** (Tu ne smeš parkirati.)
say.de: **mustn't** (must not) sagt: Es ist nicht erlaubt, du darfst nicht. Vorsicht, das ist nicht *du musst nicht*: **You mustn't feed the horses.** (Du darfst die Pferde nicht füttern.) **You mustn't smoke in the barn.** (In der Scheune darfst du nicht rauchen.) **can't** sagt oft dasselbe: **You can't park here.** (Hier darfst du nicht parken.)
say.it: **mustn't** (must not) dice che non è permesso: **You mustn't feed the horses.** (Non devi dare da mangiare ai cavalli.) **You mustn't smoke in the barn.** (Nel fienile non si fuma.) **We mustn't be late.** (Non dobbiamo fare tardi.) **can't** spesso dice lo stesso: **You can't park here.** (Qui non puoi parcheggiare.)
say.en: **mustn't** (must not) says it is not allowed: **You mustn't feed the horses.** **You mustn't smoke in the barn.** **We mustn't be late.** **can't** often says the same: **You can't park here.**

examples.de: Du darfst die Pferde nicht füttern.
examples.it: Non devi dare da mangiare ai cavalli.

examples.en: You mustn't smoke in the barn.
examples.de: In der Scheune darfst du nicht rauchen.

say.sl: **don't have to** pomeni, da ni treba; lahko, če hočeš: **You don't have to pay.** (Ni ti treba plačati.) **She doesn't have to get up early on Sunday.** (V nedeljo ji ni treba zgodaj vstati.) Torej **You mustn't go.** (Ne smeš iti.), **You don't have to go.** (Ni ti treba iti.) Britansko je tudi **You needn't pay.**
say.de: **don't have to** sagt: Es ist nicht nötig, du musst nicht: **You don't have to pay.** (Du musst nicht zahlen.) **She doesn't have to get up early on Sunday.** (Am Sonntag muss sie nicht früh aufstehen.) Also **You mustn't go.** (Du darfst nicht gehen.), aber **You don't have to go.** (Du musst nicht gehen.) Britisch auch: **You needn't pay.**
say.it: **don't have to** dice che non è necessario, ma puoi se vuoi: **You don't have to pay.** (Non è necessario pagare.) **She doesn't have to get up early on Sunday.** (La domenica non è costretta ad alzarsi presto.) Quindi **You mustn't go.** (Non devi andare, è vietato.), ma **You don't have to go.** (Non sei obbligat{m:o|f:a} ad andare.) Britannico anche **You needn't pay.**
say.en: **don't have to** says there is no need; you may if you want: **You don't have to pay.** **She doesn't have to get up early on Sunday.** So **You mustn't go.** means don't go, but **You don't have to go.** means go if you like. **You needn't pay.** is British too.

say.sl: **should** + osnovna oblika, brez to in brez -s, je nasvet, mehkejši od must: **You should take a coat.** (Bolje, da vzameš plašč.) **You shouldn't walk alone on the fell.** (Ni pametno, da greš sam{m:|f:a} na hrib.) **Should I call the doctor?** (Naj pokličem zdravnika?) **What should I do?** (Kaj naj naredim?)
say.de: **should** + Grundform, ohne to und ohne -s, gibt einen Rat, weicher als must: **You should take a coat.** (Du solltest einen Mantel mitnehmen.) **You shouldn't walk alone on the fell.** (Du solltest nicht allein auf den Berg gehen.) **Should I call the doctor?** (Soll ich den Arzt rufen?) **What should I do?** (Was soll ich tun?)
say.it: **should** + la forma base, senza to e senza -s, dà un consiglio, più morbido di must: **You should take a coat.** (Dovresti prendere un cappotto.) **You shouldn't walk alone on the fell.** (Non dovresti andare da sol{m:o|f:a} sul monte.) **Should I call the doctor?** (Chiamo il medico?) **What should I do?** (Che cosa devo fare?)
say.en: **should** + the base form, with no to and no -s, gives advice, softer than must: **You should take a coat.** **You shouldn't walk alone on the fell.** **Should I call the doctor?** **What should I do?**

examples.en: It's cold on the fell. You should take a coat.

translation.sl: Dobrodošli v gostilni! To so pravila. Tukaj moraš biti ob osmih. Sam mora priti ob sedmih, ker pripelje pivo. V kuhinji ne smeš kaditi: to ni dovoljeno. Tal ti ni treba pomivati: ni treba, to naredi babica Maggie. Moraš delati ob nedeljah? Ne. In v ponedeljek vzemi plašč. Moj nasvet: mrzlo bo!
translation.de: Willkommen im Gasthaus! Das sind die Regeln. Du musst um acht hier sein. Sam muss um sieben kommen, weil er das Bier bringt. In der Küche darfst du nicht rauchen: Das ist nicht erlaubt. Die Böden musst du nicht wischen: Das ist nicht nötig, das macht Oma Maggie. Musst du sonntags arbeiten? Nein. Und am Montag solltest du einen Mantel mitnehmen. Mein Rat: Es wird kalt!
translation.it: Benvenut{m:o|f:a} alla locanda! Queste sono le regole. Devi essere qui alle otto. Sam deve venire alle sette, perché porta la birra. In cucina non devi fumare: non è permesso. Non è necessario lavare i pavimenti: lo fa nonna Maggie. Devi lavorare la domenica? No. E lunedì dovresti prendere un cappotto. Il mio consiglio: farà freddo!
translation.en: Welcome to the inn! These are the rules. You have to be here at eight. Sam has to come at seven, because he brings the ale. You mustn't smoke in the kitchen: that's not allowed. You don't have to wash the floors: there's no need, Granny Maggie does that. Do you have to work on Sundays? No, you don't. And you should take a coat on Monday. My advice: it's going to be cold!

translation.en: Do you have to feed the sheep today, Jack? — Yes, I do. And Meg has to stay with me. — You look tired. You should rest. — I can't. But I don't have to get up early tomorrow: it's Sunday!
